labels.label: prop:K_calcul
labels.notes: Corollary beyond the target, cited unmarked. SFABTZ.K_calcul's conclusion is the paper's three assertions verbatim with sing₀(M) = SFALocal.sing M 0: (a) ∀ p ∉ sing₀, K⁺ = I⁺ ∧ K⁻ = I⁻; (b) ∀ p ∈ sing₀, K⁺ = I⁺; (c) IsCausal → ∀ p ∈ sing₀, K⁻ = J⁻ ∖ {p}. It is the curated Causal.Causality.K_calcul (curation row prop:K_calcul) with every named hypothesis discharged: PushUp (SFALocal.pushUp), Z⁺ = M (SFALocal.mem_Zplus), M ∖ sing₀ ⊆ Z⁻ (SFALocal.mem_Zminus_of_notMem), SingularPastAt on sing₀ (SFABTZ.singularPastAt), FirstCountableTopology from the charts. Remaining hypotheses are only the E≥0-manifold reading (DEC-25 ruled; OQ-18, OQ-82, OQ-34 open); Hausdorff and second countability weakened away. No `line`. Hypotheses witnessed with a BTZ point at M = E₀ (nonvacuous_e0's first two conjuncts). Lean ≥ paper under the readings.

findings.what: « They are not chart facts alone »: this is stated as a fact, but the Lean only shows that the proofs use causal arc-connectedness and push-up. Nothing formalized shows that the two fields fail without absolute minimality. The existing precedent, SFALocalE0.e0_topTotal_separates (refutes I⁻(p) = ∅ without minimality, row rem:btz_pas_tarentin), does not refute these two fields: with ≤_⊤ and ≪_⊤ total, SingularPastAt and Iplus_of_lt both hold. By hand, a causality on E₀ that adds one relation x ≤_⊤ p (x regular, p BTZ) and agrees on proper open sets would break SingularPastAt (ii) at x, but this is not formalized.

findings.what: The finding is true but understated. The file proves that some suitable sequence exists. An audit probe (/tmp, deleted, standard axioms) proves more from this file's exists_chart, exists_below and mem_interior_Jplus: at every BTZ point p of every E≥0-manifold, p ∈ Int J⁺(u) for EVERY u ∈ J⁻(p) ∖ {p}. So the proof's arbitrary increasing sequence p_n ∈ J⁻(p) ∖ {p} already meets lem:K_facile's hypothesis, and the gap at l.1570 is one of justification only.

question.asked: Is defi:causal_E0 a statement only of the model E₀, or also of the BTZ points of an E≥0-manifold? Reading taken: at the model, E0.causal_E0; at M, the two fields plus J⁻(p) ⊆ the component; the literal half-line not read at M.
question.assessment: Not genuinely open, so no OQ-87. (1) The printed text settles the scope of the main assertions: « for a singular point p ∈ sing(E₀) ». The model form is E0.causal_E0, under OQ-34/OQ-35. (2) The definition's only M-level sentences are its « In particular » consequences. At M they are rem:btz_pas_tarentin's content, a done row (SFALocal.btz_pas_tarentin), and the not-past-distinguishing sentence. OQ-35 already reads that sentence at M (« extreme BTZ white hole » = a BTZ point, sing₀ ≠ ∅), and finding 4 gives it at every E≥0-manifold. (3) Transferring the model facts to M as global fields is the strict library's audited modelling choice (Causal/SingularFlat.lean, BTZAxioms docstring and SCOPE: « The BTZ facts of defi:causal_E0 are stated globally, as the proofs of prop:K_monotone and cor:K_injectif use them »). DEC-64 ruled the corrected l.1352–1355 at exactly that level. The causality at M is OQ-18. (4) The literal half-line at M is a mathematical fact, not a reading: given `line`, it holds when M is causal (SingularFlat.Jminus_eq_image), and it fails when M is not causal. No ruling would change a statement or a mark of this row, which stays unmarked on OQ-34/OQ-35 and DEC-64 in any case. Record the reading as a note, not as an OQ.
question.by_hand_check: True, by hand (not formalized). τ ↦ τ + T preserves −2dτdr + dr² + r²dθ², and the library's chart transitions near the axis include tauShift (BPrimeE0.exists_eqOn_rotE0_tauShift), so E₀/⟨τ + T⟩ is an E₀-manifold: Hausdorff and second countable, since the ℤ-action on ℝ × ℂ is free and properly discontinuous. Its BTZ points form the circle {r = 0}. Every point q of the circle has a lift q̃ below a lift p̃ of p on the axis, and the projected axis segment is causal, so q ≤ p. Together with J⁻(p) ⊆ sing₀ (mem_sing_zero_of_le) this gives J⁻(p) = the whole circle. SingularPastAt holds there: J⁻(u₀) = J⁻(p) = the circle, and p ∈ Int J⁺(u_n) from the chart. The manifold is not causal. The phenomenon is already disclosed in SingularFlat's SCOPE (Causal/SingularFlat.lean:76–80, « E_α or E_0 modulo a translation along its singular line: the component is a circle »).
